entries.en: The card arrived promising a service nobody was running
entries.body_en: The first draft said "scan if found for safe contact". Nothing was connected to it, so the promise was empty.
entries._audit_body_en: The arriving package printed 'Scan if found for safe contact, no address shown' on both faces and carried a QR encoding https://wish-it-better.network/c/REXI-008, a host this project does not run. A finder scanning a lost dog's tag would have reached nothing. Resolved by re-pointing the QR at this page (verified by tools/qrdecode against the composed face, not the source PNG) and rewriting the card to say what it is: a demonstration.

entries.en: The chip cannot go through the printer, so the card makes room for it
entries.body_en: NFC stickers are not inkjet safe. The card prints a 25 mm circle and you stick the tag on afterwards.
entries._audit_body_en: No NTAG inlay is rated for an inkjet card printer's ink path. Rather than pretend otherwise, one face reserves a printed 25 mm circle sized for an NTAG215 wet inlay, drawn 1 mm proud so a slightly-off placement still lands inside a printed ring rather than over the type. NTAG215 specifically: 504 bytes of user memory, which is what makes a self-contained URL fragment payload fit at all. NTAG213's 144 bytes do not.

entries.en: Seven faces, because choosing the picture is the whole job
entries.body_en: Other cards here have two fixed faces. A pet tag has one real decision, so this page lets you try every pairing.
